---
title: "Analysis"
subtitle: "How we measure what an inversion recovered. Each metric is defined once here; per-run values are on the Results pages."
---

The metrics apply to both [checkerboard tests](../results/index.qmd) and the [field-data inversion](../results/field/index.qmd). For checkerboards there is a known true model to compare against. For field data there isn't one, so comparison metrics need a reference model such as Slab2 or a published velocity model.

Code: the cell *"Quantitative checkerboard recovery: SSIM + companion metrics"* at the end of [`checkerboard_3D/evaluate_checkerboard_results.ipynb`](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography/blob/main/checkerboard_3D/evaluate_checkerboard_results.ipynb). Metrics are computed on each horizontal depth slice (10–200 km), in percent velocity perturbation relative to the starting model.

## Ray coverage

### What it is

How well each part of the model is sampled by the data. Regions that no ray crosses cannot be resolved, so recovery is only meaningful inside the covered region.

### How it's calculated

The current code uses a **proxy**: it doesn't trace rays, but marks a cell as covered if the inversion changed the model there.

1. Take the absolute recovered perturbation $|I|$ (in %) on a depth slice.
2. Average it over a moving window about one checker cell wide (21 × 21 km for the 20 km checker on the 1 km grid).
3. Mark the cell **covered** where that local average exceeds 0.05 %.
4. Drop the padded model edges.

$$
\text{frac\_covered} = \frac{\#\{\text{interior cells with } \overline{|I|}_{\text{window}} > 0.05\%\}}{\#\{\text{interior cells}\}}
$$

The same mask restricts where SSIM and the companion metrics below are computed.

### What the number means

| Output | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `frac_covered` | 0–1 | Fraction of the map area at this depth that the inversion updated. 0.77 means 77 % of the slice was touched by the data; 0 means none of it. |

### Limitations and planned improvement

- Because it is built from the result, the mask can't separate "not sampled" from "sampled but the data asked for no change".
- It doesn't distinguish crossing rays from many parallel rays, which resolve structure very differently.
- A data-independent alternative is already sketched in [`forward_modeling.ipynb`](https://github.com/ajm-glitch/AlaskaTomography/blob/main/checkerboard_3D/forward_modeling.ipynb) (commented out): applying the adjoint of the linearized Eikonal operator to a vector of ones gives each cell's total ray sensitivity. Binning ray directions per cell would add a crossing-angle measure.

## SSIM (structural similarity)

### What it is

An image-comparison score [@wang2004] that asks whether the recovered slice has the **same pattern** as the true one, window by window. It is more sensitive to shape than a single correlation over the whole map.

### How it's calculated

For each small window (about one checker cell wide) at the same position in the true slice $T$ and the recovered slice $I$, SSIM compares three things:

$$
\text{SSIM} = \underbrace{\frac{2\mu_T\mu_I + C_1}{\mu_T^2 + \mu_I^2 + C_1}}_{\text{mean (luminance)}}
\cdot \underbrace{\frac{2\sigma_T\sigma_I + C_2}{\sigma_T^2 + \sigma_I^2 + C_2}}_{\text{contrast (amplitude)}}
\cdot \underbrace{\frac{\sigma_{TI} + C_2/2}{\sigma_T\sigma_I + C_2/2}}_{\text{structure (pattern)}}
$$

- $\mu$, $\sigma$, $\sigma_{TI}$ are the window means, standard deviations and covariance.
- $C_1 = (0.01L)^2$ and $C_2 = (0.03L)^2$ are small stabilizers, with $L = 10$ (the −5 % to +5 % range of the anomaly).
- The window values form a local SSIM map. The reported number is its mean over the covered region.

Depths where the true pattern is flat are skipped. The checkerboard varies as $\cos(\pi z / L_{\text{checker}})$ with depth, so it is zero at nodal planes (for a 20 km checker, every other 10 km slice), and there is nothing to compare.

### What the numbers mean

| Output | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ssim_masked` | −1 to 1 | **Main score.** Mean SSIM inside the covered region. 1 = identical; 0 = no similarity; negative = pattern reversed (anomalies with flipped sign). |
| `ssim_interior` | −1 to 1 | Same, over the whole model interior, so unsampled areas pull it toward 0. |
| `ssim_amp_corrected` | −1 to 1 | SSIM after rescaling the recovered slice to the true amplitude. Isolates **pattern** recovery from amplitude loss: if this is much higher than `ssim_masked`, the shape is right but too weak. |
| `pearson_r` | −1 to 1 | Correlation between true and recovered values inside the mask. Ignores amplitude. |
| `recovery_ratio` | ≈ 0–1 | $\sum t\,i \,/\, \sum t^2$: fraction of the true amplitude recovered. 1 = full amplitude, 0.12 = 12 %. Typical for damped, smoothed inversions to be well below 1. |
| `nrms` | ≥ 0 | $\lVert i - t \rVert / \lVert t \rVert$. 0 = perfect; 1 = no better than predicting no anomaly; above 1 = worse than that. |
